thumbnail_text_variants.label: ARM A — modern
thumbnail_text_variants.strategy: IDENTICAL text on both arms — same words, same size, same position. Text is the constant; only the world changes. A win must be attributable to the imagery or it teaches nothing carryable.

thumbnail_text_variants.label: ARM B — traditional
thumbnail_text_variants.strategy: Same text as Arm A. The two arms hold the HUMAN MOMENT constant (woman alone at dawn, warm cup in both hands, open book) and vary only the world around it — contemporary room vs Mughal palace terrace. That pairing is what makes the result interpretable.

thumbnail_prompt:
TWO ARMS — matched pose, opposite worlds. Identical text block on both: 'SET THE DAY RIGHT' in large dark-teal serif, right third, with a second tier beneath reading 'Sitar · Raga Ahir Bhairav · 432Hz'. Same framing, same text size and position, same border weight.

ARM A (MODERN): Contemporary lifestyle illustration, clean and airy. One woman in simple modern loungewear seated by a large window in early-morning light, holding a warm mug in both hands, an open journal and a small vase of flowers beside her. Warm white, soft sage, pale oak palette. Minimal, generous negative space, modern wellness aesthetic. One figure only.

ARM B (TRADITIONAL): Pichwai/Kangra miniature on aged parchment with ornate gold and deep-teal border. One Indian woman in a cream-and-gold sari seated on a Mughal pavilion terrace at sunrise, holding a brass cup in both hands, an open book and a brass vase of flowers beside her. Palace and river soft in the distance. THIN THE CLUTTER to match Arm A's density: drop the diya, drop the lotus bowl, keep only cup + book + one vase.

⚠️ Neither arm shows a sitar being played. Our own data: performer thumbnails convert WORST (Grounding, sitar player, CTR 3.03) while viewer-in-their-own-morning converts best (Start Your Day Strong, waking in bed, 6.11; Positive Morning Vibes, jogging with earbuds, 5.57). A sitar may rest at frame edge; it must not be the subject.
thumbnail_ab_note: THIS IS THE EXPERIMENT — Studio Test & Compare, 2 thumbnails, 1 title. First time the channel has ever varied the IMAGE: all 40+ prior A/B tests varied thumbnail TEXT only. ⚠️ ON CONCLUSION: pull the COUNTRY SPLIT per arm before reading the winner. If traditional wins in India and modern wins in T1, that is a geography lever, not a losing arm — and it is the read the T1 push needs.
description:
Morning Routine Music | Slow Sitar & 432Hz | 1.5 Hours of Calm, Unhurried Start

Some mornings you wake up already behind. The phone is in your hand before your feet are on the floor, and the day starts pulling at you before you have had a chance to arrive in it.

This peaceful Indian ambient meditation music is designed to slow the first hour down — to give you something steady to move through your morning alongside, instead of rushing at it.

Enjoy 1.5 hours of gentle sitar melodies blended with a soft tanpura drone, light tabla and warm ambient textures, tuned to 432Hz and looped seamlessly so nothing interrupts you.

Perfect for morning routines, waking up gently, stretching, journaling, yoga, morning meditation, making coffee, getting ready for work, quiet reading, light housework, or simply sitting still before the day begins.

🎵 ABOUT THIS MUSIC
Instrument: Sitar, with tanpura drone and light tabla
Raga: Ahir Bhairav — a traditional early-morning raga, warm and gently uplifting
Style: Indian classical ambient, instrumental only
Mood: Calm, steady, quietly positive
Atmosphere: Soft dawn light, unhurried
Tuning: 432Hz
Duration: 1.5 hours

🎧 HOW TO USE
Put this on as soon as you wake, before you reach for anything else. Keep the volume low enough that it sits underneath the room rather than filling it. Headphones deepen the tanpura drone, but this works just as well through a speaker while you move around.

⏱ CHAPTERS
0:00 — First light
9:00 — Waking gently
18:00 — Settling into the morning
27:00 — Steady and unhurried
36:00 — Warmth building
45:00 — Clear and open
54:00 — Moving through the hour
63:00 — Quiet momentum
72:00 — Soft continuation
81:00 — Carrying the calm forward

⏱ BEST FOR
Waking up without rushing
Morning routines and getting ready
Stretching and gentle yoga
Morning meditation
Journaling and planning the day
Making breakfast or coffee
Quiet reading before work
Light housework
Easing morning tension
Starting the day with a clear head

If this music helped you start the day calmer and less rushed, subscribe to Raga Focus for more uninterrupted Indian ambient healing music.

suno_prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals — gentle Indian classical sitar in Raga Ahir Bhairav with soft light tabla, warm rounded tone, unhurried steady morning character around 70 BPM, calm positive energy, seamless loop.
suno_prompt_note: Short one-liner per the banked default (~205 chars). NO 'slow' anywhere — morning lane, and 'slow' makes Suno generate draggy output that costs retention; the BPM number sets tempo. Tabla included per the Sitar rule (tabla for Sitar, none for Bansuri/Surbahar). 432Hz is NOT in the prompt — it is applied in post (see production_spec), because Hz tags in the prompt degrade generation.

experiment.type: thumbnail A/B (image is the variable — a channel first)
experiment.hypothesis: h_2026-08-02_thumb_cultural_register (new): the cultural WORLD of the thumbnail gates click-through, and gates it differently by geography. Modern/contemporary imagery converts T1; traditional Indian imagery converts India. Held constant: the human moment (woman alone at dawn, warm cup, open book) and the entire text block.
experiment.why_not_a_replica: Deliberately NOT two variants of a known winner. Replicating the 6.11%/5.57% morning composition would say which replica is better, not whether the visual language itself is the ceiling. User directive 2026-08-02: 'copying something does get us new winners but trying a hypothesis will.'
experiment.read_at: d7 — CTR per arm, then COUNTRY SPLIT per arm
experiment.caveat: ~20K first-week impressions is near the power floor (Test #41 came back underpowered, #42 was voided). The two arms differ on palette, density and century as well as culture, so read it as package-level.
experiment.next_test: Figure count — 1 vs group. Live prior: Morning Energy (6 figures) is the #2 video but its 3.88% CTR is BELOW the 4.71% channel average, i.e. it won on distribution, never shown to convert. Run it where a group reads naturally.
